QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_41

question.text: Chapter 12 refers to the 'blind-pool nature of AIF investing' as a rationale for which investor behaviour?

answer.text: Investors must set the risk profile of their investment at the time of commitment, since portfolio holdings cannot be easily adjusted or rebalanced later due to illiquidity.
Investors should not perform any monitoring since they cannot see the pool.
Investors must demand daily NAV updates to compensate for blindness.
Investors should invoke termination rights at every quarterly review.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12: 'Because of the blind-pool nature of AIF investing (ignoring co-investments), it is crucial for investors to set the risk profile of their investment at the time of commitment. Moreover, given AIF's lack of liquidity, the investor cannot easily adjust portfolio holdings or rebalance them.' The Trap: Option B contradicts the very monitoring chapter. Option C pushes daily NAV (Cat III leakage). Option D is an overreaction rarely used. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Distributor) emphasises the same point when matching a client's risk profile. XIX-C covers the Manager-side framing identically. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching LPs, disclose the TOP-3 portfolio sector tilts you plan to pursue (not specific companies) and the drawdown schedule. LPs who commit with realistic expectations on blindness are less likely to withhold Fund II capital.
